bannedNote.en: Prohibited in competition when applied from a standing position: the arm is trapped under tori's armpit and the elbow has nowhere to go, so uke cannot submit in time, and the IJF penalises it with hansoku-make. On the ground it is a legal armlock, and it is taught, demonstrated and examined: the BJA sets it as a 1st Dan fundamental skill.

about.en: The armpit armlock: uke's straight arm is clamped under tori's armpit and levered against the elbow with the whole body. Powerful and fast, which is why applying it as a standing technique is prohibited in competition; on the ground it is applied with particular care. Competition joint locks are restricted to the elbow and to senior age groups; learn and practise this only under instruction.

en: Their wrist gripped with both hands, arm clamped under your armpit
Their thumb points up; your body, not your arms, applies it
Ground technique only in competition; standing application is banned
On the ground beside your partner, take their extended right arm at the wrist with both hands, their thumb turned upward.
Clamp their arm under your right armpit so your side and upper arm press along the back of their elbow.
Keep their wrist tight to your chest, their arm straight, your body side-on to theirs.
Apply by turning your trunk slowly away from their head, the whole body levering the elbow against your armpit.
This lock arrives fast, so apply it more slowly than any other: small movement, constant attention, instant release at the tap.

receiving.en: Your wrist is taken in both hands and your arm vanishes under their armpit, their whole body now framing your elbow; the leverage is severe and arrives with very little movement. Tap clearly at the first hint of pressure; this lock gives the least warning of any, and an elbow or shoulder can be injured before the pain becomes severe. Never snatch out of a lock with a twist.

viNotes.en: Prohibited standing because the arm has nowhere to go and uke cannot submit in time, and that concern is sharper again when neither of you can see the arm. On the ground, take the wrist in both hands, clamp the arm along your side, and turn your trunk by the smallest amount that produces anything at all. Apply this more slowly than any other lock in judo.
